newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks move in narrow range in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks move in narrow range in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were mixed and moving in a narrow range in early Tuesday morning trade, with most brokers expecting the market to drift lower.
"The market could basically do anything," said James Robinson, vice president at Salomon Brothers. "We are in the lap of the gods."
The Hang Seng Index was 15 points or 0.13 percent higher at 12,641 after opening 12 points down. Turnover was HK$1.37 billion.
"But we are probably going to drift lower today," Robinson added.
The Dow Industrials slid 43.34 points to 6,660.21 overnight, largely in reaction to comments by U.S. Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin about the possibility of the U.S. economy overheating.
"I am very bullish on the Hong Kong market," said a broker at Asia Equity. "But I think those remarks could bring us down today as they did the U.S. Treasury market."
The 30-year long bond fell overnight to yield 7.09 percent at the close in New York.
Asia Equity expected the market to rise to 15,000 or higher in the second half of the year, the broker said.
Properties initially outperformed other blue-chip sectors then fell back. H shares rallied strongly from the open.
Sun Hung Kai Properties leapt HK$1.00 to HK$80.75 at the open then eased to trade HK$0.25 lower at HK$79.50. Henderson Land was unchanged at HK$65.00 after some early gains.
Cheung Kong added HK$0.50 then fell back to trade HK$0.50 lower at HK$67.75.
H share Northeast Electrical rebounded HK$0.09 to HK$1.48. The company reported a 48.75 percent fall in its 1996 earnings to 83.77 million yuan on Monday.
Shanghai Hai Xing Shipping gained HK$0.25 to HK$1.56, a new 1997 high, on heavy turnover of HK$310.12 million. The company recently reported a loss of 157.47 million in 1996.
Hang Seng Index futures pulled the market lower in mid morning. The April contract dropped 90 points to 12,535 in active trade.
